title: Relative perfection of scheme complexes under arbitrary base change
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a flat locally finitely presented morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], let $g:S'\to S$ be arbitrary, and let $b:X'=X\times_SS'\to X$ and $f':X'\to S'$ be the projections [def-pc-fibre-product]. Work with Zariski structure sheaves and unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-pc-derived-category]. Suppose $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ is pseudo-coherent [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex] and locally has finite Tor dimension over $S$: each point has an open neighbourhood on which its restriction, as a complex over $f^{-1}\mathcal O_S$, has finite Tor amplitude [def-pc-finite-tor-dimension-over]. Then $Lb^*E$ [def-pc-derived-pullback] is pseudo-coherent and locally has finite Tor dimension over $S'$ with respect to $f'$. No flatness of $g$, Noetherianity, properness or global uniform Tor interval is required.

source.place: Tag 0DI5, lemma-base-change-relatively-perfect, with relative perfection defined by Tag 0DI0, definition-relatively-perfect.

proof.text: Fix $x'\in X'$ with images $x\in X$, $s'\in S'$ and $s\in S$. Choose affine neighbourhoods $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $s$, $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $x$ inside $f^{-1}V$, and $V'=\operatorname{Spec}R'$ of $s'$ inside $g^{-1}V$, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Then $U'=U\times_VV'$ is an open neighbourhood of $x'$ in $X'$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], and is $\operatorname{Spec}A'$ for $A'=A\otimes_RR'$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Restrictions of $E$ to $U$ remain pseudo-coherent by its local-model definition. Its locally finite relative Tor dimension remains so over $V$: at a point of $U$, the stalk of the inverse-image base ring is still $\mathcal O_{S,f(x)}$. The stalk criterion [lem-trf-ringed-tor-amplitude-stalk-test] therefore preserves each local interval on restriction.

source.place: Tag 0DI5, lemma-base-change-relatively-perfect, first proof; affine localization in Tag 0DI2, lemma-affine-locally-rel-perfect.

proof.text: The ring map $R\to A$ is flat. Under the open immersions of $U$ and $V$, the restriction $U\to V$ of $f$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the section map $R\to A$, by the affine adjunction [lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction]. Hence, for every prime $\mathfrak q\subset A$ over $\mathfrak p\subset R$, the compatible stalk identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-stalk-localization] identify $R_{\mathfrak p}\to A_{\mathfrak q}$ with the stalk map of $f$. It is flat by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Apply [lem-pc-affine-sections-flat-over-base] to $M=A$ to conclude. Pseudo-coherence gives quasi-coherent cohomology by [lem-sc-pseudo-coherent-qcoh]. Use [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] and [lem-pc-affine-pseudo-coherent-criterion] to represent $E|_U$ by $\widetilde Q$, where $Q$ is a bounded-above complex of finite free $A$-modules. By [lem-trf-affine-relative-tor-amplitude-criterion], $Q$ restricted to $R$ has Tor amplitude in some interval $[a,b]$. This interval is chosen on $U$, not on all of $X$.

source.place: Tag 0DI2, lemma-affine-locally-rel-perfect; Tag 0DHY, lemma-tor-dimension-rel-affine; Tag 08E7, lemma-pseudo-coherent-affine; algebra.tex Tag 00HT, lemma-flat-localization (6).

proof.text: Each term of $Q$ is flat over $A$, and flat over $R$: it is a finite direct sum of copies of the flat $R$-module $A$, and its tensor functor is the corresponding finite direct sum of exact functors. Thus [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] applies over both rings. By [lem-pc-affine-kflat-pullback-chart-comparison], the affine pullback of $E|_U$ to $U'$ is represented by $\widetilde{Q'}$ with $Q'=A'\otimes_AQ$. In every degree $A'\otimes_A A^{r_i}=(A')^{r_i}$, with differential the same matrix after applying $A\to A'$. Hence $Q'$ is bounded above and finite free. The reverse implication of [lem-pc-affine-pseudo-coherent-criterion] shows that this pullback is pseudo-coherent.

source.place: Tag 0DI5 first proof and Tag 08DW, lemma-quasi-coherence-pullback; more-algebra.tex Tag 064K, lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism, and Tag 0650, lemma-pull-pseudo-coherent.

proof.text:
As an $R'$-complex, $Q'$ is isomorphic to $R'\otimes_R Q$ by [lem-pc-base-tensor-ordinary-iso], whose degreewise map sends $r'\otimes q$ to $(1\otimes r')\otimes q$. Since $Q$ is K-flat over $R$, this represents $Q\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'$. Choose a bounded flat $R$-complex $F$ supported in $[a,b]$ representing the restricted $Q$, using [lem-pc-module-tor-amplitude-flat-model]. Both models are K-flat by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat]. Apply the functor $-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'$ of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] to their isomorphism in $D(R)$; its computation clause identifies the resulting isomorphism in $D(R')$ with
$$\operatorname{Res}_{R'}Q'\simeq R'\otimes_R F.$$
Every term of the latter is flat over $R'$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change], and it is zero outside $[a,b]$. The reverse implication of [lem-pc-module-tor-amplitude-flat-model] now gives the same Tor interval over $R'$ for $Q'$. This uses no flatness of $R\to R'$.

source.place: Tag 0DHW, lemma-base-change-relatively-perfect; Tag 0661, lemma-base-change-comparison; Tag 066L, lemma-pull-tor-amplitude; Tag 0654, lemma-tor-amplitude; Tag 06Y6, lemma-derived-base-change. The comparison is written in D(R-prime).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-affine-relative-tor-amplitude-criterion] to $R'\to A'$ and $Q'$. Its interval equivalence shows that $\widetilde{Q'}$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ over the inverse-image structure ring from $V'$. The composite maps $U'\to X'\to X$ and $U'\to U\to X$ agree. The composition isomorphism of [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-pullback-composition] therefore identifies the computed affine pullback with $(Lb^*E)|_{U'}$; for an open immersion the termwise restriction is exact and the tensor formula for [def-pc-derived-pullback] is ordinary restriction. Also $\mathcal O_{V',s'}=\mathcal O_{S',s'}$, so the stalk criterion [lem-trf-ringed-tor-amplitude-stalk-test] identifies this relative interval with the one over $(f')^{-1}\mathcal O_{S'}$ on $U'$. Since the chosen neighbourhoods cover $X'$, the local-model definition proves pseudo-coherence of $Lb^*E$, and these intervals prove locally finite relative Tor dimension. The intervals may vary with $U'$. Empty schemes give a vacuous cover, and the zero complex allows $[0,0]$.

lean.statement: theorem relativePerfect_baseChange [∀ Z : Scheme.{u}, HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Z.toRingedSpace))] [∀ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (U : Z.Opens), HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings Z.toRingedSpace).over U))] {X S S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (g : S' ⟶ S) (E : schemeDerivedCategory X) (hE : IsPseudoCoherent X E) (hTor : ∀ x : X, ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ HasFiniteTorDimensionOver (U.ι ≫ f) ((derivedPullback U.ι).obj E)) : IsPseudoCoherent (pullback f g) ((derivedPullback (pullback.fst f g)).obj E) ∧ ∀ x' : (pullback f g : Scheme.{u}), ∃ U' : (pullback f g : Scheme.{u}).Opens, x' ∈ U' ∧ HasFiniteTorDimensionOver (U'.ι ≫ pullback.snd f g) ((derivedPullback U'.ι).obj ((derivedPullback (pullback.fst f g)).obj E))
